opening: Falstaff decides to improve his finances by seducing two married women who can access their husbands' money. He economises on effort by sending them nearly identical letters. Unfortunately for him, the women compare notes and find the proposal more useful as entertainment than temptation. Shakespeare brings his great opportunist into a town where household intelligence can defeat swagger, while a jealous husband supplies additional confusion. The comedy belongs to people who understand exactly how they are being underestimated and decide to make the experience expensive.
